research_concepts: units with lift threshold (>=70% positive, median >2pp)
methodological_questions: What defines a 'unit' (team-season, defender-season, or matchup) and is the 70% share computed over a fixed unit set?
How is 'PNR fail' defined from play-by-play without using outcome-derived labels (for example, points or turnovers) that would leak the result into the classification?
What is the baseline for lift: league-average PULL_UP points per possession, or a context-matched expectation (shot distance, clock, personnel, matchup)?
What sample per unit is needed for a stable lift estimate, and how many units are there after applying minimum exposure rules?
How are shot quality, personnel, and matchup confounders controlled when comparing PULL_UP outcomes after PNR fail?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned zero records (n_results = 0), so no earlier study by this project on this question is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: No prior lift estimates for PULL_UP after PNR fail exist in the retrieved evidence.
No information on whether the 70% / 2pp thresholds were used, justified, or tested before.
No information on unit definitions, minimum exposure rules, or sensitivity results from earlier work.
own_inferences: The conjunctive threshold (>=70% of units with lift>0 and median lift >2pp) is only meaningful once 'unit' and 'lift' are fixed; as posed it is underspecified.

The data (play-by-play with shot distance and results, plus derived play-type records) is probably sufficient to estimate a league-pooled PULL_UP lift after PNR-type defensive breakdowns, so the main obstacle is definitional rather than data volume.

Using only complete data (2022-23 to 2024-25 regular and playoff seasons, and the 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13) avoids partial-season bias; the 2025-26 playoffs are partial as of 2026-05-23 and should be excluded.
uncertainties: Whether the PNR-fail classification can be derived from pre-shot observables without using points or turnovers as the label.
How many team-season units have enough PNR-fail possessions with PULL_UP attempts to give stable estimates.
Whether the derived play-type records in the graph database were validated against raw play-by-play.
Whether the 2pp threshold is in points per possession or in shooting percentage, which changes the scale of the test.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records, so no historical finding changed the decision. The decision rests on the task statement and the data description alone.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR fail must be defined from pre-possession or pre-shot observables; if it is defined by the points or turnover result, the lift is partly built into the label.
Per-unit PNR-fail plus PULL_UP counts may be too low for stable unit-level lift, especially for the 2025-26 partial-season or single-season units.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved (n_results = 0), so it cannot be determined whether this question has been answered. Nothing is cited.

risks.text: If PNR fail is defined by a scoring or turnover outcome, the lift measured afterward is partly circular.
Using full-possession or full-game information to assign units or labels could leak future outcomes into the classification.
Many team-season units may have too few PNR-fail possessions with a PULL_UP attempt to estimate lift reliably.
With 30 teams across about four seasons, the >=70% share criterion and median threshold may be decided by noise rather than a real effect.
Shot distance, shot quality, personnel, matchup, and clock/score context can change PULL_UP efficiency and PNR-fail frequency together.
Derived play-type records from the graph database may not match raw play-by-play classifications; labeling errors would bias lift.
PULL_UP points per possession are probably similar across units, so a 2pp threshold may be close to the league-wide baseline variation.
Testing several play-type counters and several unit definitions can produce a passing threshold by chance.
Shot-selection and offensive trends change across 2022-23 to 2025-26, which can shift the PULL_UP baseline over time.
Without placebo play types, a positive lift may reflect general shot-value differences rather than a counter effect.
Joining play-by-play events to possession records and season/playoff splits can introduce duplication or misaligned possessions.

design.estimand: Per-possession points difference (PULL_UP minus a context-matched expected baseline) for possessions that follow a pre-specified PNR-fail event, estimated separately for each unit and pooled across the league.
design.unit: Team-season (offense or defense, as pre-registered), with a minimum count of PNR-fail possessions containing a PULL_UP attempt set before analysis. Defender-level units are a secondary analysis.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13 only). Playoffs reported separately as a sensitivity analysis. Exclude the 2025-26 playoffs, which are partial as of 2026-05-23.
design.power: Not computed; a pre-analysis simulation is required, with the minimum units count and per-unit PNR-fail/PULL_UP counts fixed in advance. Report the number of units meeting the minimum.
design.controls: Context-matched expected baseline using shot distance bins, clock and score state, period, shooter and defender identity (random effects), and lineup/personnel indicators. PNR-fail classification uses only information available before the PULL_UP shot. Compare against league-average expected values.
design.falsification: Placebo counters (for example, post-up or spot-up after PNR fail) with the same lift and threshold rules; permutation of PNR-fail labels within game; and a check that a 2pp threshold is not reached under shuffled labels.
design.multiplicity: One primary hypothesis (the 70% share and median >2pp criteria). Other play types and unit definitions are secondary and exploratory, with a correction such as Holm applied across the reported family.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) at least 70% of qualifying units have a lift estimate above 0, and (b) the median unit lift is above 2pp, with the bootstrap 95% CI for the median excluding 2pp from below, and both criteria hold in the held-out season. Rejected if the CI for the share or the median is entirely on the failing side. Otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 through 2024-25 (regular and playoffs) and 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13. Graph-database derived play-type records must be validated against raw play-by-play before use, and the snapshot date recorded (2026-05-23).

methodological_questions: Does PULL_UP lift after PNR fail exceed 0 in at least 70% of units with median lift above 2pp?
How should units be defined and lift measured without outcome-derived labels or lookahead leakage?
What sample size and exposure is needed per unit for a stable lift estimate?
How to control confounding by shot quality, personnel and matchup when estimating counter lift?
args.query: Historical evidence on whether PULL_UP shots are a league-wide counter to PNR failures in NBA play-by-play data, including unit definition, lift estimation, thresholds, and prior failed approaches

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
